question: The first Women's Cricket World Cup was hosted by which of the following countries?
solution:
When was the first Women's ODI World Cup played? The correct answer is__** England.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The first Women's Cricket World Cup was hosted by England in 1973. While the first men's World Cup was in 1975.**
 
• The tournament was played in a round-robin format with four teams - **England, Australia, New Zealand, and Jamaica.**
 
• England emerged as the champions by winning all three of their matches, while Australia finished as runners-up with two wins.
 
• The Women's Cricket World Cup is held once every four years and the current champions are England, who won the 2017 edition held in England and Wales.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Australia has hosted the Women's Cricket World Cup twice, in 1988 and 2009.**
 
• West Indies has never hosted the Women's Cricket World Cup, but they did co-host the men's event in 2007 along with three other countries.
 
• **New Zealand has hosted the Women's Cricket World Cup thrice, in 1982, 2000, and 2022).**
 
• The eighth iteration of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup competition took place in 2023.
 
• It took place in South Africa from February 10–26, 2023.
 
• The tournament concluded in Cape Town.
 
• After defeating the home team, South Africa, by 19 runs in the championship match, Australia claimed their sixth and third consecutive title.
 
• It featured a total of 7 teams, including two unique teams – Young England and International XI, which usually do not feature in regular World Cups. 
 
• Each match was of 60 overs, which was different from today's 50-over format.
 
• This tournament proved to be a milestone for women's cricket – it showed that women can also compete at the international level.
 
• Many young girls were inspired to play cricket from this tournament, making the future of women's cricket bright.
 
• Behind this event was the hard work of some dedicated cricket lovers, who made it a success despite the lack of resources.
